mechanism_claims.claim_text: Galaxamide analog anticancer potency varies with the d-amino-acid position; Analog-6 has the lowest IC50 values across the four tested cancer cell lines in Table 1.

supports: Table 1 IC50 matrix and results text compare Galaxamide and Analog-1 through Analog-6.

mechanism_claims.limitations: This is an in vitro cancer-cell cytotoxicity/SAR claim, not antimicrobial potency.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Analog-6 induces apoptotic phenotypes in HepG2 cells, including sub-G1 accumulation, Annexin V/PI early-apoptotic staining, and nuclear condensation/fragmentation after 48 h exposure.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=2.2.2; xml:sec=2.2.3; xml:sec=2.2.4; xml:fig=3; xml:fig=4; xml:fig=5; supp:Figure S1
supports: Primary text and figures report sub-G1 cell-cycle effects, early apoptosis by Annexin V/PI, and Hoechst nuclear morphology changes.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanism evidence is limited to HepG2 cells and the assayed concentrations/time point.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Analog-6 activates a mitochondria-mediated apoptotic pathway in HepG2 cells, supported by increased cleaved caspase-3, caspase-9, and PARP in Western blot experiments.
direct_assay_types: Western blot for cleaved caspase-3, caspase-9, and PARP

supports: Results text reports increased cleaved caspase-3, caspase-9, and PARP with Analog-6 concentration; methods describe Western blot procedure.

mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper infers mitochondrial-pathway involvement from apoptosis-marker Western blots; it does not directly measure mitochondrial membrane potential in the local text.

caution_findings.note: No antimicrobial mechanism is supported by this primary paper; mechanism claims are limited to anticancer/apoptosis assays in HepG2 cells.
Mitochondria-mediated pathway is reported in the paper from apoptosis marker Western blots; direct mitochondrial potential measurements were not found in local text.
